text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> service: inference-embeddings-eu, urgency: high. Alert: embedding queue latency spike + 5xx rate increase. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-5239 — auto-notify oncall.

Priya K: acked. I'm on it, joining bridge. Seeing alerts in SLO dashboard: tail latency > 2s and ~4% 502s for the last 90s. Customer impact: some customer ingestion jobs failing, a handful of downstream requests getting 5xx.

Jon S: I'm jumping in — curious if this is a capacity issue or a routing problem. Any recent deploys to embedding workers?

Priya K: No deploys in last 30m. Autoscaler triggered but didn't add capacity fast enough. I'm going to try a manual scale and enable fallback routing to warm pool.

Ava M: adding logs: top errors look like 'grpc: upstream connection reset' and kv cache misses spiking. Suspect IO saturation on a subset of nodes in eu-west-1.

Priya K: running manual scale now:

```bash
kubectl --context=prod-eu scale deployment embedding-worker --replicas=18 -n redwood-prod
```

Priya K: scaled to 18, rolling up pods. pinging metrics.

Daniel R: if IO is saturated, adding replicas might worsen disk contention — recommend shifting some inference routing to the hot-warm fallback pool (fallback-model: embed-medium-quant). I can run the route command.

Jon S: good call. If we flip traffic to fallback-model for non-SLA customers, we can buy time. How fast can we change routing?

Daniel R: ~15s to push the policy. running:

```json
{"route":"inference-embeddings-eu","policy":"fallback:embed-medium-quant","scope":"non-enterprise"}
```

Daniel R: pushed policy. non-enterprise traffic now using fallback. 

Priya K: tail latency dropping to ~700ms for fallback traffic. 502 rate trending down. Customer success ping: @Customer Success — we rerouted non-enterprise traffic to fallback model, enterprise unaffected.

Ava M: host-level IO still noisy on node-pool-3, cordoning one node to drain for investigation.

Priya K: cordon/drain commands:

```bash
kubectl cordon node/eu-worker-3
kubectl drain node/eu-worker-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

Priya K: node drained. starting pod reschedule. metrics show recovery for previously impacted pods.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident status updated -> acknowledged (Priya K).

Jon S: ok great. Priya, can you handoff ownership when things are stable? I'll take postmortem and look at long term automations (faster scaling + IO detection).

Priya K: planning to hand off to Jon in ~30m after stability window. Current status: mitigated for majority of traffic, elevated monitoring. Running 30m stability check per runbook.

Daniel R: adding follow-up actions to ops board: investigate IO pattern on node-pool-3, consider node storage performance baseline and autoscaler cooldown tuning.

Ava M: also capturing logs for the pods that saw resets: /var/log/pods/embed-*/stderr.log saved to s3://incidents/5239998888/logs\. Link: https://s3.example/5239998888/logs\.

Priya K: status update: last_message_ts check-in -> 5239998902. Stability window started. Handoff to Jon S for post-incident follow-up. Jon, you own the postmortem + customer communication.

Jon S: taking it. I'll run the RCA and draft customer impact note. Thanks everyone — great coordination. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident resolved -> out-of-alert (auto-close disabled until postmortem completed).

Priya K: quick checklist left for handoff: 1) confirm no further 5xx for 30m 2) snapshot autoscaler metrics 3) attach drained node disk perf to ticket 4) verify fallback-policy rollback plan.

Jon S: noted. I'll open the incident ticket and assign tasks, ETA for postmortem draft: 24h.

Priya K: handing over. handing_off_to: Jon S. :white_check_mark:
